t: Section 1964(c) of title 18, United States Code, is amended by inserting before the period “, except that no person may rely upon any conduct that would have been actionable as fraud in the purchase or sale of securities to establish a violation of section 1962. The exception contained in the preceding sentence does not apply to an action against any person that is criminally convicted in connection with the fraud, in which case the statute of limitations shall start to run on the date on which the conviction becomes final”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this section concerns a right to sue, since it amends the civil RICO remedy provision and mentions actions and a statute of limitations. But it only narrows a private cause of action against private defendants and sets when a limitations period starts; it does not grant any outside party a right to sue over or object to a federal decision. No outside party is consulted or involved in any federal decision-making.
fable.s: no person may rely upon any conduct that would have been actionable as fraud in the purchase or sale of securities to establish a violation of section 1962

opus.w: This amendment narrows the civil RICO cause of action between private parties and sets when the statute of limitations starts. It does not involve any federal decision or bring outsiders into one. Its mention of suits and limitations periods may look like a right to sue, but the definition counts only a right to challenge a government decision. Limiting or describing private litigation does not qualify.
opus.s: no person may rely upon any conduct that would have been actionable as fraud in the purchase or sale of securities to establish a violation of section 1962

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the statute of limitations and defines exceptions for fraud-based RICO claims. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision. The reference to a 'person' refers to a defendant in a criminal case, not a participant in a regulatory or policy process. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: except that no person may rely upon any conduct that would have been actionable as fraud in the purchase or sale of securities to establish a violation of section 1962. The exception contained in the preceding sentence does not apply to an action against any person that is criminally convicted in connection with the fraud, in which case the statute of limitations shall start to run on the date on which the conviction becomes final
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of a "person" who is "criminally convicted" implies some form of participation or right to sue. However, the text is strictly defining the scope of liability and the statute of limitations for civil RICO actions. It does not grant a new right to sue, nor does it require consultation with outsiders. The "person" mentioned is the defendant in a criminal case, not a participant in a federal decision-making process. The text is purely procedural regarding litigation timelines and exceptions to fraud-based claims.
